newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway foreign minister to visit Israel, Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Norway foreign minister to visit Israel, Hebron.

text.p: Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal leaves for Israel on Sunday in an effort to help get the peace process back on track, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Friday.

Spokesman Ingvard Havnen said Godal would meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat separately as well as other important figures on both sides. Godal would also visit the West Bank city of Hebron.
"Given the role we have in general in the peace process we have a strong interest in getting the peace process on track again," Havnen said.
Norway helped broker the 1993 Israeli-Palestinian peace pact, keeps observers in Hebron and chairs an ad hoc liaison committe of donor countries to Palestinians.
Havnen said Godal was in close contact with the United States and discussed the Middle East on the telephone with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher earlier in the day.
In Washington, U.S. government sources said Warren was expected to set off for Israel on Saturday to push forward Israeli-Palestinian peace talks following the Middle East summit this week.
